subject: Renewal request: capacity amnesty & price stability for Catalentix
messages:
From: Sam Howell <sam@catalentix.com>

Cc: accounts@catalentix.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal questions — capacity amnesty and price hold

Hi Soojin,

We’re up for renewal in August and the execs are asking for two things before we proceed: a firm price hold for 12 months from renewal and some concession for the Q1 overages we saw while we ramped a new GenAI product. The usage spike was predictable but the timing hit our budget.

Ideally Catalentix is asking for:
- a 12-month price hold at current effective SaaS rate,
- an amnesty that converts the Q1 overage into a one-time credit applied across the first three invoices post-renewal, and
- a staged-burst allowance for the first 90 days after renewal so our seasonal load doesn’t trigger penalties.

Can Redwood do this without requiring a larger long-term commit? We’re also evaluating a modest capacity uplift (roughly +25% monthly tokens). Happy to jump on a short call this week.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Howell
Head of Platform
Catalentix

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal questions — capacity amnesty and price hold

Team — forwarding Catalentix ask. Quick take: they want a price hold + convert past overage to credit + 90-day staged burst. They say they may increase commit by ~25% but don’t want to be forced into a multi-year bump.

Key constraints from our side:
- Price hold for 12 months is doable if we limit the exception to their current model family and require a small committed uplift or a nominal recurring retainer.
- Amnesty -> converting overage to credits: we can propose a full credit for 50% of the overage and offer to spread it over 3 invoices (helps cash flow).
- Staged-burst: can set a temporary burst window of +30% on top of new committed capacity, with tiered overage rates after 90 days.

Action items: Ben, can you run quick margin impact with 25% uplift + 3-month burst? Marissa, can you draft an external term-sheet that keeps them on the same list price for 12 months but ties the price hold to either (a) a small 6-month retainer or (b) a 12-month commitment at +10% volume? We should preserve ability to limit burst to model family / region.

I’ll propose an external offer that emphasizes predictability and lets them trial the uplift.

Sooj

--
Soojín Lee
Senior Account Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal questions — capacity amnesty and price hold

Sooj / Marissa,

Ran high-level numbers: if they uplift commit by 10% for 12 months and we credit 50% of the Q1 overage (their dashboard shows ~$42k overage), our net ARR impact is manageable.

Scenarios:
1) Minimal-risk: 6-month retainer ($8k/mo) + 12mo price hold. Amnesty = 50% of overage as credit spread over 3 invoices. 90-day staged burst at +30% of new commit (free inside burst), then standard overage tiers. This preserves cash and limits SLA exposure.
2) Favorable: 12-month +10% commit: full 100% credit of overage applied as invoice credits, price hold 12 months, staged burst +30% for 90 days. This is revenue-accretive vs scenario 1.

My recommendation is to lead with scenario 1 externally (lower ask to get deal done), and hold scenario 2 as a sweetener if they accept the uplift. We can also attach a short-term performance SL A to protect us on extreme bursts.

I attached a draft term outline.

Ben
